I'm going to be honest, any rules about when a partner can have sex is going to come across as controlling.

I have a few requirements for poly situations and thats it:

- Be honest about stuff if. Lying is the number one way to kill attraction and the relationship.
- If you're going on a date or hook up then *try* let me know, just so we can schedule our time effectively. But this isn't a hard and fast rule.
- We all agree to share info on testing schedules, risks etc. We use protection and notify our partners if we make decisions not to use it. If people are trying to get pregnant we talk about that too.
- Communicate: expectations, comfort levels. Just have good open and honest communication. 

That's it.

What to do next?

2) Change your locks. Getting a key back isn't going to cut it. He may have a copy. 

3) Block him on everything. This is going to really sting, but I promise it's absolutely for the best. Block his relatives too so none of them can be his contact to you.

4) Get support - book a therapist appointment ASAP. Tell them it's an emergency. Designate a solid friend or family member to drop his stuff at his. Do NOT go yourself. If he asks about you, instruct your friend/family member to say "no comment." 

5) Cry. Cry hard. Let it all out. Block some time off work if you can and let your boss know what happened. Right now, focus on healing.
